pr_title: unix/mpthreadport: Ensure enough thread stack to detect overflow.

issue_context.title: thread_stacksize1 is still occasionally failing
issue_context.body:
Even after #5784, the `thread_stacksize1` test is still failing sometimes.

Example https://travis-ci.org/github/micropython/micropython/jobs/667965401#L1801
comments: Looks like it's on the standard, 64-bit unix build.  If it's not reproducible then it's hard to fix...

I can reproduce a crash that looks very similar using FreeBSD 12.0 on a 64-bit virtual machine.  There the stack size defaults to 64k.  Using 4k instead of 2k stack size in the test gets it passing, but I'd like to understand why.

Looking into the crash under FreeBSD, it occurs in `free(th)` in `mp_thread_finish()`.  It looks like the threads allocated stack is indeed too small and executing the thread overwrites data on the C stack.

So it seems that 8192 bytes are needed for the thread stack-overflow safety margin.

review_comments: The problem with doing it that way is that it introduces a discontinuity in the amount of stack available: if you do `stack_size(2 * MARGIN - 1)` then it'll allocate `3 * MARGIN - 1`, but if you do `stack_size(2 * MARGIN)` then it'll allocate just `2 * MARGIN`.  That could lead to confusion if one is gradually increasing/decreasing the stack size and testing code.
